subject: Tranche assignation appeal — Echo Analytics priority request
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana@echoanalytics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procure@echoanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated tranche contention — urgent ask

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a sharp drop in inference throughput this week after the Helix tranche was rebalanced. Our pipeline latency spiked ~2.3x and several customer jobs missed their SLAs. We understand load is high across customers, but this coincides with the new tranche assignments that, per our account team, moved 20% of reserved capacity away from Echo's dedicated pool.

Can Redwood provide a short-term prioritization (soft-preempt or temporary tranche bump) until we complete an internal model-window reduction? If not, we need a path to guaranteed capacity — Echo is evaluating a larger commitment but needs operational assurances.

Attached: echo_capacity_snapshot_q3.pdf (PDF) — logs and perf traces.

Regards,
Dana Liu
Head of ML Platforms
Echo Analytics
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Dana Liu <dana@echoanalytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated tranche contention — urgent ask

Dana — thanks for flagging and for the snapshot. I can see the latency regressions in the logs.

Quick summary from our side: last week we applied a tranche rebalance in the Helix zone to accommodate two new committed deals (Catalyst & Meridian). That rebalance consumed a portion of the soft-reserve buffer that Echo had been benefitting from during peak windows.

I'm looping in Monica (Customer Success) and Ben (Capacity Ops) to evaluate: 1) whether we can temporarily reassign a 12 GPU equivalent tranche back to Echo for 72 hours, and 2) what the operational impact would be to existing commitments.

We should avoid a blunt preempt unless absolutely necessary — prefer a short, documented, reversible tranche swap and a call with Echo to confirm mitigation steps.

Next steps: Monica to propose operational runbook; Ben to surface the allocation waterfall and potential knock-on effects; Karthik to confirm fleet-level constraints for Helix region.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated tranche contention — urgent ask

All — reviewed Echo's traces and Rishi's notes. Proposed temporary plan:

- 72-hour soft bump: move a 12-GPU tranche labeled 'Echo-temp-72h' from the Helix soft-buffer into Echo's dedicated pool.
- Rate-limit policy: tie an autoscale cap to 85% token throughput to avoid cross-customer noise.
- Observability: add a per-route cost/latency dashboard tile and set a 10-minute alert for any SLA breach.

Operational impact: this will reduce the pool available to Catalyst by ~8% during the window; Meridian will be unaffected because it runs in a separate Helix subzone. If Catalyst is near headroom, we could trigger a canary pause and notify their AMs.

Attachments: proposed_tranche_swap.xlsx (XLSX) — contains the mapping and rollback steps.

I recommend we tell Echo we can do this as a 72-hour mitigation and schedule a technical alignment to discuss long-term guarantees (commit increases, higher-tier dedicated blocks, or multi-zone peering).

-Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 07:50:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated tranche contention — urgent ask

I ran the simulation on the Helix fleet for next two weeks. Key points:

- Moving 12 GPUs to Echo-temp-72h is feasible immediately, but we have a ~30% chance of triggering a transient throttle on Catalyst during its morning peak (02:00-04:00 UTC) on Tue/Thu.
- We can mitigate by shifting Catalyst's scheduled heavy jobs to a staggered window or by offering a 12-hour burst window from a reserve node pool (costly).
- Long-term: recommended customer-facing options are (a) upgrade Echo to a 24-GPU reserved tranche, (b) configure multi-zone affinity to reduce single-zone contention, or (c) sign a 6-month committed burst addendum.

I'm OK to proceed with the 72-hour soft bump if Catalyst AMs are notified and we publish the rollback timeline. I will prepare the automation runbooks for swap + rollback.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Dana Liu <dana@echoanalytics.com>, procure@echoanalytics.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Aug 2027 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Tranche assignation appeal — Echo Analytics priority request

Dana — thanks for your patience. We discussed internally and we can offer the following immediate remediation:

1) Temporary 72-hour tranche bump: we'll move a 12-GPU tranche (Echo-temp-72h) into your dedicated pool starting 2027-08-08T00:00:00Z. This is a soft-priority assignment — not a permanent change.
2) Observability & guardrails: we'll add a per-route latency tile and an SLA alert at 10 minutes; rate capped to 85% during the window to reduce cross-traffic impact.
3) Notification to impacted AMs: we will inform Catalyst AMs of potential 8% headroom reduction and provide a recommended staggered window to avoid peak overlap.

Action items for Echo: confirm acceptance by EOD Mon 2027-08-08 so we can schedule the swap; share any blackout windows. On our side: Ben will run the automation and Monica will join the in-call to confirm rollback triggers.

Longer term I'd like to discuss a committed 24-GPU tranche or multi-zone peering as a durable solution — we can put that on the agenda for our renewal talk. We recognize this is operationally sensitive; the tranche bump is a stop-gap to stabilize your production SLAs.

Attachments referenced: echo_capacity_snapshot_q3.pdf, proposed_tranche_swap.xlsx

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
